title: Verify track.objects #33 (Phase C video spine, position 20)
intro: Run the run_module item locally through Invoke-Skill.ps1 (or the Module Launcher). track.objects associates the committed 6-frame fixture's per-frame detect.objects #16 detections into identity tracks. Confirm the checklist against the produced tracks JSON, record an overall verdict + notes, and export the result. It is deterministic + parallel_safe (no model/CUDA/port); re-running yields a byte-identical tracks.json.

items.title: track.objects tracks the committed scenario fixture -> tracks JSON
items.expected: status ok; a tracks.json + tracks.md artifact. The 6-frame / 19-detection scenario yields 4 tracks (2 car + 2 person), 4 births, 1 death: track 0 & 1 are the two cars crossing (each length 6); track 2 is a person that coasts through a 1-frame occlusion (frames 0,1,3,4,5); track 3 is a person that appears mid-sequence (first_frame 1) and is aged out (aged_out true, last_frame 2). Deterministic: re-running produces a byte-identical tracks.json (same sha256).

checklist.text: track 2 (person) has frames [0,1,3,4,5] -- it coasted through the frame-2 occlusion
track 3 (person) has aged_out == true and last_frame == 2 (a death)

checklist: re-running the same input yields a tracks.json with the same sha256 (byte-identical / deterministic)

items.title: Confirm determinism + parallel_safe by inspection
items.action_text: Run the item above twice and compare the two runtime/artifacts/<id>/tracks.json files' sha256 (they must match). Confirm the manifest declares parallel_safe:true, gpu:none, models:[] -- there is no CUDA/model/loopback-port binding, so it is safe to run alongside other CPU workers.
items.expected: Two runs -> identical tracks.json sha256. Manifest: parallel_safe true, gpu none, no models, no network.
checklist: the two tracks.json files are byte-identical (same sha256)
skill.json: parallel_safe == true, requirements.gpu == none, requirements.models == []
